text:
Kavya Rao: Thanks for the great questions in today's all-hands runtime section. I'm capturing the follow-ups here so we don't lose action items.
Diego Morales: Quick clarifying Q: when you said p95 goals, were those measured on 8k tokens or 4k? Need to align our perf tests.
Kavya Rao: Good catch. The hosted p95 target 120ms is measured at steady-state for 8k context with typical request lengths (avg 512 tokens). Dedicated committed instance SLA target is 100ms p95 for the same 8k profile.
Priya Patel: Are we standardizing on int8 profiles for targets? Some teams benchmark with fp16 and it's confusing.
Kavya Rao: Targets assume our default quantized serving path (int8 or 4-bit where applicable). FP16 remains supported but will show higher ms — we estimate +10-25ms depending on model and kernel.
Eli Turner: On batching strategy, can we get more detail on the 'latency_budget' heuristic? There were regressions when aggressive batching was enabled.
Kavya Rao: Plan is a hybrid approach: latency-first batching — accumulate until either max_batch_size or latency_budget_ms. Then a separate workload-tier allows more aggressive batching for throughput-oriented customers. We will roll the aggressive mode behind per-route flags and a controlled canary.
Diego Morales: Can someone post the config snippet for latency_budget so I can mirror it in local emulation?
Priya Patel: tagging +1
Kavya Rao: I'll post a canonical config example in this thread today.
sre-oncall: Related ops question: KV cache eviction caused tail latency spikes for one enterprise customer. Any immediate mitigation?
Eli Turner: Short term: we can bump per-tenant cache TTLs and reduce global pressure eviction frequency. Long term: switch to LRU with protected recent prefix segment. Engineering to publish the exact eviction algorithm and expected metric deltas.
Kavya Rao: Action: Runtime team to publish eviction policy doc + rationale. We'll add metrics: eviction_count, eviction_ttl_count, eviction_pressure_count.
Diego Morales: On tracing, can we get kernel-level timings (matmul/softmax/attention) surfaced in Console? Current spans are coarse.
Kavya Rao: Yes. Runtime will add kernel-level spans (kernel_name, kernel_ms, kernel_device) behind a feature flag next sprint.
Priya Patel: Any updates on the kernel hotpatch fallback story? We had a canary where the hotpatch partially applied and some requests hung.
Eli Turner: We implemented safe-fallback logic in 0.9.x that should route to compatible kernel variants. If requests hung that's probably a coordination/ack bug in the hotpatch roll path. Please drop trace ids.
Priya Patel: Example traces: trace-2026-11-04-101 and trace-2026-11-04-107.
Eli Turner: grabbing those now.
Diego Morales: ETA on AOT/vectorized attention kernels? That would help the p95 a lot.
Kavya Rao: Prioritized Q2. Rough internal timeline: planning 2w, prototype 3w, canary 4w. We'll share perf expectations and a migration checklist soon.
Priya Patel: Can we get a short readiness checklist for teams (model validation, custom ops, route flags, monitoring)?
Kavya Rao: Yes — I'll post a concise checklist by EOD. High level: 1) confirm model compatibility with new kernels; 2) run eval baselines; 3) adjust per-route batch configs; 4) enable canary flags and monitor kernel_failure_rate and tail-latency.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: runtime/kernel-vector-proto -> canary group beta (job 9042) :rocket:
sre-oncall: tagging release-war-room for visibility. We'll watch p95/p99 and error budgets during canary.
Kavya Rao: Summary of actions: Diego will run local tests with latency_budget config, Eli to investigate hang traces, Runtime to publish eviction policy and kernel spans, Kavya to post rollout checklist. Ping me here or DM if missing anything.
Diego Morales: I'll post the local config gist to #eng-runtime later today.
Priya Patel: thanks all!
Eli Turner: thanks :thumbsup:
